reason: Reproduced using installed uv 0.13.5 on Ubuntu 24.04.5, Linux x86_64, with isolated temporary files and caches. With requires-python='>=3.11', .python-version=3.11, and UV_PYTHON=3.13, `uv lock -v` selected CPython 3.13.17, while `uv audit -v --preview-features audit-command` downloaded and selected CPython 3.11.17. Adding `--python 3.13` failed with exit 2: unexpected argument '--python'. Plain `--frozen` skipped interpreter discovery; adding `--python-version 3.13` restored the 3.11 download. With dependency `requests==2.32.5; python_version < '3.12'`, the targeted frozen audit still audited five packages and reported vulnerabilities, even after repinning Python to 3.13; the equivalent uv tree command excluded requests. A Windows-only dependency likewise remained audited with a Linux target. Normal locking downloads alone do not establish a bug, but target filtering contradicts documented behavior. The exact reported uv 0.13.6/aarch64 environment was not tested. Updated $RUNNER_TEMP/issue-context/README.md with commands, evidence, limitations, and existing test coverage; checkout files and GitHub state were unchanged.
